rounds.text: Zeal Global Services Ltd trades at an extremely compelling valuation, featuring a P/E ratio of just 7.72x compared to a sector benchmark of 18.13x, alongside an EV/EBITDA of 3.49x [E1, E6, E11]. The underlying business quality is exceptional, demonstrated by a robust 5-year compounded sales growth of 36% and profit growth of 44%, backed by a superior ROCE of 16.6% against a sector benchmark of 6.7% [E10, E14, E17]. Furthermore, the company has dramatically strengthened its financial position by slashing borrowings from Rs 20 Cr to just Rs 2 Cr, making it almost debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x [E32, E34, E55]. This fundamental strength is validated by a rules-based screen scoring 90 out of 100, supported by positive institutional accumulation and operating margins that recently expanded by 1 percentage point year-over-year [E26, E38, E56]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth has contracted by 10% and operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative at Rs -12 Cr [E16, E30]. Nevertheless, a reverse DCF indicates that today's price of Rs 100 already implies an unrealistic -4.9% earnings growth, offering a stark disconnect from the company's historical growth trajectory [E2, E42].

While headline valuation metrics appear low, a deeper examination reveals severe cash flow strains and deteriorating top-line momentum that undermine the investment case [E16, E30]. Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has contracted by 10%, highlighting a sharp deceleration from historical rates [E16]. More concerningly, the company experienced a massive cash drain in March 2026, generating negative operating cash flow of Rs -12 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -15 Cr, leading to a dismal cash conversion ratio of -1.09x against reported profit [E29, E30, E31]. Operating margins have also compressed by 2 percentage points over a three-year period to 8% in the TTM, accompanied by an inconsistent yearly margin trend [E25, E27]. Furthermore, the stock carries high volatility of 57.9%, a negative Sharpe ratio of -0.01, and has suffered a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -79.1%, underscoring extreme price risk [E48, E49, E50]. Conceded: [E32].

The bear points to top-line contraction over the trailing twelve months [E16], but ignores the powerful longer-term context of 36% compounded sales growth over 5 years and 37% over 3 years [E14, E15]. Conceded: [E30, E31] on the negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -12 Cr and Rs -15 Cr in March 2026; however, this cash drain coincides with a dramatic de-leveraging where borrowings plummeted from Rs 20 Cr down to just Rs 2 Cr by September 2026 [E34]. Furthermore, capital expenditure proxy CWIP sits at Rs 0 Cr down -100%, indicating that capex is largely completed and new capacity is coming online [E35]. Regarding margin compression [E25], quarterly performance demonstrates a rebound with operating margin rising to 8% in September 2026 compared to 7% in the year-ago period [E26]. Finally, the bear's focus on high volatility and historical drawdowns [E48, E49] overlooks the technical reality that the price trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 [E45, E46].

The bull leans on 5-year and 3-year compounded sales growth of 36% and 37% [E14, E15], but fails to address the immediate reality of top-line contraction with a -10% compounded sales growth rate over the trailing twelve months [E16]. Conceded: borrowings fell from Rs 20 Cr to Rs 2 Cr by September 2026 [E34], but this debt reduction coincided with an alarming operational cash drain, yielding a negative operating cash flow of Rs -12 Cr and a negative free cash flow of Rs -15 Cr in March 2026 alongside a severe cash conversion ratio of -109x [E29, E30, E31]. While the bull points to completed capital expenditure and zero CWIP [E35] as a sign of incoming capacity, this transition has failed to prevent longer-term profit deceleration, evidenced by 3-year compounded profit growth collapsing to just 4% [E18]. Conceded: the operating margin ticked up to 8% in September 2026 from 7% in the prior year [E26], but the yearly and quarterly trends remain explicitly inconsistent and the TTM operating margin has compressed by 2 percentage points over three years to 8% [E25, E27, E28]. Finally, citing moving averages and relative strength [E45, E46] does not erase the severe structural volatility and price risks inherent in an asset carrying an annualised volatility of 57.9%, a Sharpe ratio of -0.01, and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -79.1% [E48, E49, E50].
